description:
Modern people, including myself, have been tempted to look back at thinkers like Plato as if they were so charmingly confused it’s almost a burden we have to put up with an intellectual culture that historically took them serious.

It sounds insane to a modern person that Plato believed in pre-existent “Ideas” of which all the physical things of the world are but shades.

But this idea becomes less absurd when you realize that Plato ultimately was talking in part about the very undeniably real world of perception and consciousness and the nous.

title: A World of "Forms": Was Plato Mad?

description:
Consciousness is not physical.

That is almost a truism, but I want people to understand what that means. Consciousness is not material. The conscious world does not share an ontology with material objects—atoms “bouncing around” against each other. We can say the brain is physical: it is a physical thing with physical properties that can be pointed out in the physical universe. The brain can be measured in size or weighed, we can determine its vector and speed of movement as it is ontologically matter. Consciousness is not like this.

Consciousness is also not an emergent property of matter. This is significantly more difficult for people to acknowledge, but is ultimately no more trivial.

title: Consciousness Is Not Physical.

description:
Of course there are AI projects that have open source code. Many do, even some of the largest and most influential.

My question is somewhat deeper. Does having an libre or “open source” AI (meaning large language models) really come with the ethical and practical benefits of traditional free-software programs?

Does it really mean we know how an AI is computing something?

Does it really mean we can understand the AI’s output?

Does it really mean we have control over the program outside of ad hoc limitations?

No. In all cases.

AI is only peripherally source code.

What I mean by this is that a traditional program’s source code can be read my a competent programmer and changed as needed. There is exactly a one-to-one relationship between the source code and the program’s behavior in a given circumstance.

title: Can AI ever really be "Open Source?"
